explain.say: Here is a puzzle. In 2010 two countries had big earthquakes just six weeks apart. The stronger one killed far fewer people. How can that be? Look at the board: Haiti on the left, Chile on the right.

explain.say: Look at Haiti. In January 2010, a magnitude 7.0 quake struck close to the capital, Port-au-Prince, and not very deep. Many homes were heavy concrete with little steel inside, and they fell. More than 100,000 people died. Can you see why the buildings mattered so much?

explain.say: Now Chile. In February 2010, a magnitude 8.8 quake hit. Each step up the magnitude scale means about 32 times more energy, so this one released around 500 times more. Yet about 525 people died. Chile has strict building rules because quakes are common there.

explain.say: So why did Haiti suffer more? See the reasons lighting up: poverty, which means less money for strong buildings, no building rules, a quake right beside the city, and few hospitals and rescue teams. Which reason do you think mattered most?

faq.q: Why did so many buildings fall in Haiti?
faq.a: Many buildings were concrete blocks with little or no steel and weak foundations, and building rules were not enforced. The quake was shallow and close to the crowded capital, so the shaking was violent where most people lived.
asks: Why did the Haiti earthquake kill so many people?

faq.q: Why did fewer people die in Chile?
faq.a: After the giant 1960 earthquake, Chile brought in strict building rules, so most buildings bent instead of collapsing. It also has trained emergency services, regular drills and more money to spend on safety.
asks: How did Chile prepare for earthquakes?

faq.a: Magnitude measures the energy an earthquake releases. Each whole step up means about 32 times more energy, so a magnitude 8 is far more powerful than a 7.
asks: Is a magnitude 8 much bigger than a 7?

faq.q: What causes most deaths in earthquakes?
faq.a: Most deaths come from buildings collapsing, not from the shaking itself. Landslides, tsunamis and fires after the quake can also cause many deaths.

faq.q: What was the strongest earthquake ever recorded?
faq.a: The strongest ever recorded was magnitude 9.5, in Valdivia, Chile, in 1960. It also sent a tsunami across the Pacific to Hawaii and Japan.

facts: Haiti's earthquake of 12 January 2010 had magnitude 7.0; Chile's of 27 February 2010 had magnitude 8.8.
The strongest earthquake ever recorded was magnitude 9.5 in Valdivia, Chile, in 1960.
Each whole step on the magnitude scale releases about 32 times more energy.
